reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n and every real n-by-n positive-definite matrix A (symmetric, with strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector), the centered Gaussian measure on real n-dimensional Euclidean space with covariance A inverse equals the measure with density sqrt(det A) / (2 pi)^(n/2) times exp(-(x transpose A x)/2) with respect to canonical Euclidean volume. The Gaussian measure here is the pushforward of the canonical standard Gaussian under the linear map given by the positive-semidefinite square root of A inverse. The exponent n/2 uses real division, and the square root is the nonnegative real square root. The equality is equality of measures; the displayed real density is embedded in the nonnegative extended reals.
